run.question:
Our US prod cluster is having a checkout incident — investigate using
app-262-prod-logs.

report.summary: The index the question names, app-262-prod-logs, is the only index in the registered Elasticsearch and holds exactly 5 documents inside the authorized 24h window (2026-11-22T07:52:38Z to 09:22:38Z). Three of them are level=ERROR and carry cluster=production-us-east-1 (2 from checkout-service, 1 from payment-service); the other two are level=INFO and carry cluster=production-eu-west-1 (checkout-service). The US-prod error texts, which are exact diagnostic evidence, form a chain: checkout-service failed POST /api/checkout at 07:52:38Z with 'payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)'; payment-service logged 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 08:52:38Z; checkout-service then logged 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)' at 09:22:38Z. The deepest cause the evidence names is the external payment provider stripe-us not answering /v1/charges within payment-service's 30s client timeout, so I name stripe-us as the origin, with checkout-service and payment-service recorded as affected because each produced its own error log. The conclusion is partial, not supported, because the provider's own state is unobservable: there is no Service or Endpoint named stripe-us in the Kubernetes cluster I can read, and Prometheus and Jaeger both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or trace evidence could be checked and the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh alert's firing state is unknown. Important cluster-identity caveat: the Kubernetes cluster my access reads is not production-us-east-1 - its single node is opspilot-m1-control-plane (providerID kind://docker/opspilot-m1) with no region label, and its Prometheus alert rules carry cluster: opspilot-m1. In that readable cluster payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n are Running and ready, and their retained logs (payment 08:04:24Z-09:52:46Z, checkout 09:24:13Z-09:51:21Z) record continuous successful charges and 'payment went through' with no matching error text, so they are checked-and-healthy counter-evidence for that cluster only, not for production-us-east-1. All otel-demo containers I inspected (payment, checkout, flagd) terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 reason Unknown and restarted; that change is unexplained and could not be tied to the US-prod errors. The flagd ConfigMap shows every fault-injection flag, including paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable, at defaultVariant off at query time, which is counter-evidence against an enabled flag-injection cause for the observed 30s upstream timeout.

claims.text: app-262-prod-logs is the only index in the registered Elasticsearch (docs.count 5) and a query over the full authorized window returned exactly 5 documents, with min timestamp 2026-11-22T07:52:38.000Z and max 2026-11-22T09:22:38.000Z.

Of the 5 documents in app-262-prod-logs, 3 are level=ERROR with cluster=production-us-east-1 (2 from service=checkout-service, 1 from service=payment-service) and 2 are level=INFO with cluster=production-eu-west-1 (both from checkout-service).
In cluster production-us-east-1, checkout-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T07:52:38Z: 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (Stripe-US)'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, payment-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T08:52:38Z: 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms'.
In cluster production-us-east-1, checkout-service logged level=ERROR at 2026-11-22T09:22:38Z: 'Circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 44%)'.

The originating fault named in the evidence is the external payment provider stripe-us: payment-service's own error states its call to stripe-us /v1/charges timed out at 30000ms, and checkout-service's errors name the payment provider (Stripe-US) response timeout and then a circuit breaker on payment-service, i.e. the checkout errors are downstream of the payment-to-stripe-us timeout rather than a checkout defect.

The two INFO documents come from checkout-service in a different cluster, production-eu-west-1, reporting 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms' at 08:52:38Z and 'Healthy: success rate 99.7%' at 09:22:38Z; they are a different entity from the failing production-us-east-1 checkout-service, so they neither clear the US cluster nor provide a comparable latency baseline for it.

In the readable Kubernetes cluster (namespace otel-demo) the checkout and payment Deployments each report 1 ready/1 available replica, and pods payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n are phase Running with container ready=true.

In the readable Kubernetes cluster, payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d's retained log lines from 2026-11-22T08:04:24Z to 09:52:46Z (335 lines read) consist of 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' pairs continuing through 09:51:21Z, and a filtered read of the same container for error|fail|timeout|stripe|unavailable|circuit matched only one unrelated line, 'MetadataLookupWarning: ... incorrect Metadata-Flavor header' at 08:04:24Z; this shows no charge failure on that pod, and applies only to this readable cluster.

In the readable Kubernetes cluster, checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n's retained logs from 2026-11-22T09:24:13Z to 09:51:21Z show repeated successful PlaceOrder sequences ('payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' followed by 'order confirmation email sent'), with no error, timeout or circuit-breaker line in the retained output.

The previous container instances of checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n, payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d and flagd-d6485586b-9t42n all terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 and reason 'Unknown' (started 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z), each pod now showing restartCount 2 and owner ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87 / payment-6f7bc865d6 / flagd-d6485586b respectively.

The readable Kubernetes cluster's only node is opspilot-m1-control-plane with providerID kind://docker/opspilot-m1 and no topology.kubernetes.io/region label, and the loaded alert rule CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh carries cluster: opspilot-m1, so that cluster's identity is not the production-us-east-1 / production-eu-west-1 labelling used in app-262-prod-logs.

The 30 Services returned for the readable cluster include payment and checkout as ClusterIP services on port 8080 but none named stripe-us, and the returned Endpoints show ready addresses for the otel-demo services including payment (10.244.0.5:8080) and checkout (10.244.0.7:8080), so stripe-us is not an in-cluster Service of that cluster.

The simultaneous 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z container terminations (exitCode 255, reason Unknown) did not cause the US-prod checkout errors: the production-us-east-1 error stream starts at 07:52:38Z, before that restart, the same payment and checkout pods log successful charges after it, and those pods belong to the opspilot-m1 cluster rather than production-us-east-1.

A fault-injection flag in the flagd demo.flagd.json is not supported as the cause by the current configuration: every flag, including paymentFailure ('Fail payment service charge requests n%') and paymentUnreachable ('Payment service is unavailable'), has defaultVariant 'off', and the observed failure is a 30s upstream timeout to stripe-us rather than an injected percentage of charge failures or an unreachable payment service.

The 30s timeouts may originate in the US payment-service's egress/DNS path to the provider rather than inside the provider itself; the log text ('Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms') cannot distinguish an unresponsive provider from a blocked or degraded network path, and no egress policy, DNS or provider-side signal could be read.

While checkout-service's circuit breaker to payment-service is open at a 44% failure rate, PlaceOrder in production-us-east-1 presumably still fails fast; the index holds no document after 09:22:38Z, so recovery status is unverified.

Obtain stripe-us provider status/latency for 2026-11-22T07:45Z-09:30Z and check egress/DNS from the production-us-east-1 payment pods to the provider, since the provider is outside the readable cluster and its own state was not observable.

Once Prometheus is reachable, quantify payment charge error ratio and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds for payment's calls toward the provider, and read checkout PlaceOrder error ratio against the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh threshold (above 50% of checkout PlaceOrder server spans in error over 5m, for 2m).

gaps: Prometheus is unreachable in this Run: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no error-rate, latency or up-target series and no firing-alert state (including CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh) could be observed; missing series are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger is unreachable in this Run: traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the checkout -> payment -> stripe-us span chain, span error statuses and durations could not be checked.

The Kubernetes cluster my access reads is not confirmed to be production-us-east-1: its node is opspilot-m1-control-plane (kind://docker/opspilot-m1) with no region label and its alert rules are labelled cluster: opspilot-m1, so I cannot attribute its pod states and logs to the US-prod cluster named in the question.

stripe-us itself is unobservable here: it has no Service, Endpoint, pod or metric series in the readable cluster, so whether it was slow, failing, or unreachable over the network path cannot be verified.
No NetworkPolicy objects were returned for the readable cluster (the query returned no objects, status no_data), so egress-policy state and coverage are unknown rather than absent.

The flagd ConfigMap reflects only the state at query time; whether paymentFailure or paymentUnreachable was enabled earlier in the window and switched back off is unknown (the change_history integration is not available).

The cause of the simultaneous 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z exitCode 255 / reason 'Unknown' container terminations across otel-demo pods is undetermined; retained events cover only 09:21:00Z-09:51:14Z and only app-102/default objects, so this change cannot be placed as affected or explained.
Whether checkout-service's circuit breaker to payment-service later closed is unknown: app-262-prod-logs contains no document after 2026-11-22T09:22:38Z.

Customer/order impact beyond the two checkout-service error lines (e.g. failed checkouts volume, revenue, frontend 5xx) is unverified; no metrics, traces or frontend-proxy logs were obtainable for the production-us-east-1 cluster.
next_steps: Check stripe-us (Stripe US) incident/status history and provider-side /v1/charges latency for 2026-11-22T07:45Z-09:30Z.
From the production-us-east-1 payment pods, verify egress path, DNS resolution and any egress proxy/gateway health toward the provider endpoint.

Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access and read checkout PlaceOrder error ratio, payment charge error ratio and payment client duration for the window, plus whether CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh fired.
Inspect audit/change history for flagd flag toggles (paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) around 2026-11-22T07:52Z, since the change history integration is not available in this Run.
Review why all otel-demo containers under the readable opspilot-m1 cluster terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 reason Unknown (node/container-runtime restart suspected, unproven).

content:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
